title: School Buses
skipReason: For school bus drivers only — not needed for Class A commercial trucking
summary: Danger zones, mirror systems, loading/unloading timing, railroad crossings, and evacuation rules.

topics.heading: The danger zone
bullets: Extends up to 30 feet from the front bumper (the first 10 feet is the most dangerous), 10 feet from each side, and 10 feet behind the rear bumper.
The left side of the bus is always considered dangerous because of passing traffic.

topics.heading: Four mirror systems
bullets: Flat mirrors (left/right front corners): should show about 200 feet (4 bus lengths) behind the bus, the sides, and the rear tires touching the ground.
Convex mirrors (below the flats): wide-angle view of the sides, but distort size and distance.
Crossover mirrors (front corners): show the danger zone directly in front of and beside the bus that you can't see directly.
Overhead inside mirror: monitors student activity inside the bus.

topics.heading: Loading timing
bullets: Activate alternating flashing amber lights about 200 feet (roughly 5-10 seconds) before the stop.
Turn on the right turn signal about 100-300 feet (roughly 3-5 seconds) before pulling over.
Stop with the front bumper at least 10 feet from the students — this forces them to walk into your view.
Put the transmission in park (or neutral) and set the parking brake at every stop.

topics.heading: Unloading & road-crossing
bullets: Have students exit and walk at least 10 feet away from the side of the bus to a point where you can plainly see them.
Students crossing in front of the bus should stop at the front-right corner, check for your signal, and cross only when you signal it's safe.
Never back a school bus with students outside of it.

topics.heading: Railroad crossings
bullets: Stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail.
Turn off radios and silence passengers, open the service door and driver's window, and look/listen for a train.
Cross in a low gear and never change gears while crossing.
If your bus stalls or gets trapped on the tracks, evacuate everyone immediately — move away from the tracks AND toward the direction the train would come from.

topics.heading: When you must evacuate
bullets: The bus is on fire or there's a threat of fire.
The bus is stalled on or next to a railroad crossing.
There's an imminent danger of collision, or a need to evacuate quickly because of a hazmat spill.

topics.heading: Other numbers to know
bullets: A school bus can have up to 3 feet of tail swing — check your mirrors during turns.
Backing is strongly discouraged; if unavoidable, post a lookout, signal for quiet, and back slowly.

quiz.q: How far can the danger zone extend from the front bumper of a school bus?
quiz.explain: Up to 30 feet in front, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous; 10 feet on each side and behind.

quiz.q: Which side of a school bus is always considered dangerous, due to passing traffic?
quiz.explain: The left side is always dangerous because of passing vehicles.

quiz.q: Properly adjusted flat mirrors should let you see about how far behind the bus?
quiz.explain: About 200 feet, or roughly 4 bus lengths.

quiz.q: When approaching a stop, you should activate alternating amber warning lights about how far (or how many seconds) before stopping?
quiz.explain: About 200 feet, or 5-10 seconds, before the stop.

quiz.q: You should stop the school bus with the front bumper how far from waiting students?
quiz.explain: At least 10 feet, so students must walk into your clear view.

quiz.q: After unloading, students crossing in front of the bus should walk to a point how far away, in your view?
quiz.explain: At least 10 feet away from the side of the bus, where you can plainly see them.

quiz.q: How far from the nearest rail should a school bus stop at a railroad crossing?
options: It should not stop at all
quiz.explain: Same as buses generally: 15 to 50 feet from the nearest rail.

quiz.q: If your school bus stalls on railroad tracks, you should:
options: Try repeatedly to restart it before evacuating
Evacuate everyone immediately, moving away from the tracks and toward the train's direction
Wait for a lookout before acting
Stay inside with hazard lights on
quiz.explain: Get everyone off and clear immediately — moving at an angle away from the tracks and toward the oncoming train direction.

quiz.q: Which of these requires a mandatory bus evacuation?
options: A flat tire on level ground
The bus is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad crossing
quiz.explain: Fire/threat of fire, stalling on tracks, imminent collision, and hazmat spills all require evacuation.

quiz.q: How much tail swing can a school bus have during a turn?
quiz.explain: Up to 3 feet — check mirrors before and during turns.

quiz.q: Backing a school bus with students outside of it is:
options: Fine as long as you use a lookout
quiz.explain: Never back a school bus while students are outside it.

quiz.q: Crossover mirrors are used to see:
options: Only the interior of the bus
The danger zone directly in front of and beside the bus, invisible to direct vision
Only the rear of the bus
Traffic behind you at highway speed
quiz.explain: They cover blind areas right in front and to the sides that direct vision can't reach.

quiz.q: While crossing railroad tracks in a bus, you should:
quiz.explain: Cross in a low gear and never shift while crossing.

quiz.q: The right turn signal should be activated roughly how far before pulling over to load students?
quiz.explain: About 100-300 feet, or roughly 3-5 seconds, before pulling over.

title: Vehicle Inspection Test
examFocus: Pre-trip inspection — practice after you get your permit and start trucking school
summary: What the examiner watches for during the hands-on pre-trip inspection, including the exact numbers for the brake checks.

topics.heading: How the test works
bullets: You must point to or touch each item, name it, and explain to the examiner what you're checking and why.
A vehicle with components that are labeled or marked cannot be used for this test.
This test must be passed before you can move on to the basic control skills test.

topics.heading: Engine compartment & cab checks
bullets: Check for leaks, belt condition (1/2 to 3/4 inch play), oil level, coolant level, and power steering fluid — all with the engine off.
After starting: oil pressure should rise to normal quickly, air pressure should build toward governor cut-out (about 120-140 psi), and warning lights/buzzers should go out.

topics.heading: The hydraulic brake check (if applicable)
bullets: Pump the brake pedal 3 times, then hold it down for 5 seconds — the pedal must not move. Skipping either step is an automatic failure of this part of the test.

topics.heading: The air brake check (3 parts, if applicable)
bullets: 1) With air built to governor cutoff, release parking brake and hold the foot brake for 1 minute — leak must be under 3 psi/minute (single vehicle) or 4 psi/minute (combination).
2) Fan the brakes on and off — the low air warning must activate before pressure drops below 55 psi.
3) Keep fanning — the tractor protection valve/parking brake valve must pop out (close) somewhere in the 20-45 psi range.
Skipping any of these three steps is an automatic failure of this part of the test.

topics.heading: External walk-around highlights
bullets: Tread depth: 4/32 inch minimum on steering tires, 2/32 inch on all others.
Check every axle's suspension, brakes, and wheels the same way — springs, mounts, shock absorbers, slack adjusters, and brake drums/linings.
On combination vehicles: inspect the fifth wheel for grease, a closed gap, properly seated locking jaws, and secure air/electric lines.

tips.heading: Build a repeatable script, front to back
tips.body: Examiners score consistency as much as accuracy. Walk the same route every single practice run — engine compartment, cab, front axle, driver-side, rear, passenger-side, coupling, trailer — so the words come out automatically on test day instead of you trying to remember what's left.

tips.heading: Say the WHY, not just the WHAT
tips.body: Don't just say 'checking the slack adjuster.' Say 'checking the slack adjuster — if it moves more than about an inch by hand, the brakes are out of adjustment and unsafe.' Explaining the reason is worth more points than naming the part.

tips.heading: Practice the air brake check until it's muscle memory
tips.body: This is the section most manual-transmission Class A candidates lose points on simply from rushing. Time yourself doing the full 1-minute static leak check for real in practice — don't shortcut it, since the actual test won't let you either.

quiz.q: During the vehicle inspection test, you must:
options: Point to or touch each item, name it, and explain what you're checking and why
Only inspect items the examiner points out
quiz.explain: Full verbal explanation of each item is required.

quiz.q: A vehicle cannot be used for the inspection test if:
options: Its components are labeled or marked
quiz.explain: Labeled/marked components would give away answers, so such vehicles are disqualified from testing.

quiz.q: During the hydraulic brake check, you must pump the pedal 3 times, then hold it for how long?
quiz.explain: Hold for 5 seconds — the pedal should not move at all.

quiz.q: Skipping either step of the hydraulic brake check results in:
options: An automatic failure of the vehicle inspection test
No penalty if the brakes work fine
quiz.explain: Both components (pump 3x, hold 5 sec) must be performed correctly.

quiz.q: In the 3-part air brake check, holding the foot brake for 1 minute, the leak rate must stay under how much for a combination vehicle?
quiz.explain: Under 4 psi/minute for combination vehicles (3 psi/minute for a single vehicle).

quiz.q: In part 2 of the air brake check (fanning the brakes), the low air warning must trigger before pressure drops below:
quiz.explain: Before 55 psi, matching the general low-air-warning rule.

quiz.q: In part 3 of the air brake check, the tractor protection valve should pop out (close) in what pressure range?
quiz.explain: Somewhere in the 20-45 psi range, per manufacturer spec.

quiz.q: Minimum tread depth required on steering axle tires during inspection is:
quiz.explain: 4/32 inch on steer tires; 2/32 inch on all other tires.

quiz.q: During inspection, air pressure should build toward a governor cut-out of approximately:
quiz.explain: Roughly 120-140 psi, or per manufacturer specification.

quiz.q: On a combination vehicle's fifth wheel, what should you check for after coupling?
options: A visible gap between upper and lower fifth wheel
No visible gap, greased plate, and locking jaws properly seated
quiz.explain: A gap, missing grease, or unseated jaws all indicate a coupling problem.

quiz.q: The FLHSMV seven-step inspection method is used for:
quiz.explain: Florida's official pre-trip framework: approach, engine compartment, cab, lights, walk-around, signal/brake checks, then the air brake test.

title: Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test
examFocus: Backing exercises — practice after you get your permit and start trucking school
summary: The maneuvering exercises and how they're scored — encroachments, pull-ups, and 'looks.'

topics.heading: Possible exercises
bullets: Straight line backing.
Offset back to the right, and offset back to the left.
Parallel park (driver's side, and conventional).
Alley dock.

topics.heading: How scoring works
bullets: Encroachments: touching or crossing a boundary line or cone — each one counts as an error.
Pull-ups: stopping and pulling forward to reposition. Initial pull-ups aren't penalized, but too many count against you.

Outside vehicle observations ('looks'): you may exit to check your position, but must place the vehicle in neutral, set the parking brake, and exit safely (three points of contact). You get a maximum of 2 looks — except straight line backing, which allows only 1.
Final position: you must end each exercise exactly as instructed, or you'll be penalized and could fail.

tips.heading: Feather the clutch, don't ride the gas
tips.body: For every exercise here, creep-speed control comes from partially engaging the clutch (feathering) while the engine idles — not from tapping the accelerator. It's smoother, quieter, and far easier to stop precisely at the boundary line.

tips.heading: Cover the brake with your right foot between corrections
tips.body: During backing exercises, keep your right foot hovering the brake rather than resting on the floor. Manual-transmission candidates often lose a fraction of a second reaching for the brake pedal, which is exactly when an encroachment happens.

tips.heading: Set the parking brake fully before every 'look'
tips.body: If you exit to check your position, a rolling vehicle in neutral is an automatic problem. Set the parking brake completely, confirm it holds, then exit with three points of contact — every single time.

quiz.q: Bonus (manual transmission): the recommended way to creep forward or backward with precision during these exercises is to:
options: Use the accelerator pedal for fine speed control
Feather the clutch while the engine idles
Bump the vehicle in and out of gear repeatedly
Ride the brake and gas at the same time
quiz.explain: Clutch feathering at idle gives much finer control than trying to modulate the throttle.

quiz.q: Bonus (manual transmission): where should your right foot generally stay during a backing exercise?
options: Resting on the floor, away from the pedals
Hovering over the brake, ready for a quick correction
quiz.explain: Covering the brake shaves reaction time off corrections and helps avoid encroachments.

quiz.q: Which exercise allows only ONE outside vehicle observation ('look'), instead of the usual two?
quiz.explain: Straight line backing allows just 1 look; other exercises allow up to 2.

quiz.q: What counts as an 'encroachment' during the basic control skills test?
options: Taking too long to complete the exercise
Touching or crossing a boundary line or cone
quiz.explain: Each touch or crossing of a boundary/cone is scored as an error.

quiz.q: Before exiting the vehicle to take a 'look,' you must:
options: Place it in neutral and set the parking brake
quiz.explain: Neutral, parking brake set, then exit safely with three points of contact.

quiz.q: How many points of contact should you maintain when exiting the vehicle to check your position?
quiz.explain: Three points of contact while facing the vehicle during exit.

quiz.q: Are initial pull-ups penalized on the basic control skills test?
options: Yes, every pull-up counts as an error
No, but an excessive number of pull-ups will count against you
Only during the alley dock exercise
quiz.explain: Some pull-ups are expected; too many becomes a scoring issue.

quiz.q: If you don't end an exercise in the exact final position the examiner described, you:
options: Will be penalized and could fail the test
Only lose points on the alley dock
quiz.explain: Final position matters — finish exactly where instructed.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT one of the basic control skills test exercises listed in the manual?
quiz.explain: Highway merging is part of the on-road test, not the basic control skills test.

quiz.q: What is the maximum number of 'looks' generally allowed during most basic control exercises (excluding straight line backing)?
quiz.explain: Up to 2 looks for most exercises; only 1 for straight line backing.

title: On-Road Driving Test
examFocus: Road test — practice after you get your permit and start trucking school
summary: What examiners watch for on the road: turns, intersections, railroad crossings, and the general driving behaviors that get scored throughout.

topics.heading: The basics
bullets: Wear your seatbelt, obey every traffic law, and complete the route with zero accidents and zero moving violations.
If your route lacks a certain situation (like a railroad crossing), you may be asked to simulate it by explaining what you would do.

topics.heading: Turns & intersections
bullets: Check traffic in all directions, signal early, and don't coast unsafely (out of gear for longer than your vehicle's length).
Complete a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane; complete a left turn in the lane directly right of the center line on a multi-lane road.

topics.heading: Stop/start & roadside stop procedure
bullets: Signal, decelerate, and stop fully out of the traffic flow. Then: cancel the turn signal, activate 4-way flashers, set the parking brake, shift to neutral/park, and remove your feet from the pedals.
To resume: check traffic and mirrors, turn off flashers, signal left, release the parking brake, and pull out only once it's safe — don't turn the wheel before the vehicle starts moving.

topics.heading: Railroad crossings on the road test
bullets: Buses, school buses, and placarded vehicles must activate 4-way flashers approaching the crossing, stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail, and look/listen both ways.
Never stop, shift gears, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the crossing.

topics.heading: General driving behaviors scored the whole route
bullets: Clutch usage (manual transmission): always use the clutch to shift, double-clutch on unsynchronized transmissions, never ride the clutch or 'pop' it.
Gear usage: no grinding or clashing gears, and don't shift while turning or in an intersection.
Brake usage: smooth, steady pressure — no riding or pumping the brake.
Lane usage: stay off curbs and lane markings, stop behind stop lines, and move to the right-most lane when it's clear.
Steering: both hands on the wheel except while shifting.
Regular traffic checks: mirrors and traffic checked constantly, especially at and through intersections.
Turn signals: used at the right time, held through the maneuver, and canceled afterward.

tips.heading: Pre-select your gear before every intersection
tips.body: Slow, downshift, and settle into the gear you'll need to pull away in BEFORE you reach the stop line — not while you're already stopped and traffic is waiting. Arriving in the right gear is one of the biggest visible differences between a nervous and a confident manual-transmission driver.

tips.heading: One thing at a time through curves and turns
tips.body: Finish your downshifting and braking before you start turning the wheel, then steer, then get back on the throttle. Trying to shift, brake, and steer all at once is where new manual drivers stack up small mistakes.

tips.heading: If you grind a gear, don't chase it
tips.body: A single grind isn't an automatic fail — recover calmly, get the shift completed smoothly, and move on. Fumbling to fix it while distracted from traffic checks causes far more scoring damage than the grind itself.

quiz.q: To pass the on-road driving test, you must complete the route with:
options: No more than one minor accident
Zero accidents and zero moving violations
No requirement beyond finishing the route
quiz.explain: Any accident or moving violation fails the on-road test.

quiz.q: 'Unsafe coasting' during the on-road test means being out of gear for longer than:
quiz.explain: Coasting (clutch depressed or in neutral) longer than your vehicle's length counts as unsafe coasting.

quiz.q: A right turn should be completed in which lane?
quiz.explain: Finish right turns in the right-most lane.

quiz.q: During the roadside stop/start maneuver, after coming to a full stop you should:
options: Leave the vehicle in drive with your foot on the brake
Cancel the turn signal, activate 4-way flashers, set the parking brake, and shift to neutral/park
Rev the engine to signal your intent
quiz.explain: This sequence secures the vehicle properly at a roadside stop.

quiz.q: When resuming from a roadside stop, you should turn the steering wheel:
options: Before the vehicle starts moving, to save time
Only after the vehicle has started moving
Never turn the wheel during this maneuver
quiz.explain: Don't turn the wheel before your vehicle moves — steer once you're rolling.

quiz.q: While crossing railroad tracks during the road test, you must never:
options: Keep both hands on the wheel
Stop, shift gears, or change lanes while on the crossing
quiz.explain: No stopping, shifting, or lane changes while any part of the vehicle is on the tracks.

quiz.q: On a manual transmission vehicle with an unsynchronized gearbox, you are required to:
options: Never use the clutch except to start
quiz.explain: Double-clutching is required on unsynchronized manual transmissions.

quiz.q: 'Riding' or 'pumping' the brake pedal during the on-road test is considered:
quiz.explain: Smooth, steady brake pressure is expected — no riding or pumping.

quiz.q: Your hands should be on the steering wheel at all times, except:
quiz.explain: Return both hands to the wheel immediately after completing a shift.

quiz.q: If your test route doesn't include a railroad crossing, the examiner may:
options: Skip that scoring category entirely with no discussion
Ask you to simulate the situation by explaining what you would do
quiz.explain: You may need to describe/demonstrate the proper procedure verbally at a simulated location.

quiz.q: Bonus (manual transmission): before every intersection or turn on the road test, you should:
options: Shift to neutral and coast in
Downshift and settle into the gear you'll need BEFORE you arrive
Wait until you're stopped, then hunt for a gear
Keep the clutch pedal fully depressed the whole time
quiz.explain: Pre-selecting your gear before the stop line is the biggest visible difference between a smooth and a nervous manual driver.

quiz.q: During the on-road test, repeated grinding or clashing of gears is:
options: A scored gear-usage fault that can fail you if repeated
Automatically forgiven if you finish the route
quiz.explain: Each occurrence is scored; repeated grinding or a grind that creates an unsafe moment will fail the road test.

title: Test Day, Licensing & the One-Week Plan
examFocus: Test-day strategy, Florida-specific rules, and your 1-week study plan
summary: Exact test structure and passing scores, the manual-vs-automatic E restriction, CLP/ELDT rules, Florida test-day procedures, and a day-by-day plan to pass the written tests in one week.

topics.heading: The three written tests you'll take (Class A)
bullets: General Knowledge: 50 questions, need 40 right (80%). Taken by every CDL applicant.
Combination Vehicles: 20 questions, need 16 right (80%). Required for Class A.
Air Brakes: 25 questions, need 20 right (80%). Required if your truck has air brakes — a standard Class A tractor almost always does.
Endorsements add more tests: Hazmat 30 questions (need 24), Passenger / Tank / Doubles-Triples 20 questions each (need 16).
You get 2 attempts per test per day in Florida, and after a failed attempt you can review the exact questions you missed before retaking.
All knowledge tests are computerized and taken in person at a FLHSMV office or tax collector — there is no online testing.

topics.heading: Manual vs. Automatic — the E restriction
bullets: Test in an automatic (including an automated-manual / AMT like an Eaton UltraShift): you get the 'E' restriction — no manual transmission, ever.
Test in a manual: NO restriction — you can legally drive both automatic and manual trucks. This is the #1 reason to test in a manual if you can.
AMTs, semi-automatics, and any transmission that doesn't operate fully on the gear-shift-and-clutch principle count as 'automatic' for the restriction.
If you do get the E restriction, you can remove it later with a modified skills test in a manual truck — no ELDT required, and you don't redo the whole license.
Florida follows the federal rule: passing the skills test in an automatic-equipped vehicle must add the E restriction.

topics.heading: CLP, ELDT & the 14-day rule
bullets: Your CLP (Commercial Learner's Permit) is valid about 12 months, and you must hold it 14 days before taking the skills test.
Since February 7, 2022, first-time CDL applicants MUST complete Entry-Level Driver Training (ELDT) — theory, range, and road — from an FMCSA-registered provider before the skills test.
ELDT is verified electronically by FLHSMV, so you can't skip it or fake it. Get your CLP and start ELDT right away — it runs in parallel with your written-test study.
The knowledge tests are the fast part: a focused week of drilling practice tests is plenty to pass all three.
Your written-test passing scores stay valid for 1 year — that's your window to finish ELDT and pass the skills test.

topics.heading: The skills test (third-party, three parts)
bullets: Part 1 Pre-trip inspection: point to or touch, name, and explain every item. Florida uses the 7-step method.
Part 2 Basic control: Florida's exercises are Forward Stop, Straight-Line Backing, Forward Offset Tracking, and Reverse Offset Backing.
Part 3 On-road driving: turns, intersections, rail crossings, grades, and lane discipline.
Fail the pre-trip and you redo ALL THREE parts — FLHSMV asked FMCSA for an exemption and was denied in 2024. Pre-trip is the highest-stakes segment.
Florida uses state-contracted third-party test sites; Class A skills tests typically run $300–$500 and are paid directly to the tester.
The test vehicle must be a truck-tractor/semi-trailer combo with GCWR 26,001+ lbs and trailer GVWR over 10,000 lbs, with no labeled or marked components.

topics.heading: Florida test-day rules
bullets: Bring: valid Florida Class E license, Social Security number, proof of residency, DOT medical card, and your self-certification (interstate vs intrastate).
Under 21? You get the K restriction — intrastate only. Interstate driving and hazmat both require 21.
Knowledge tests are offered in multiple languages and can be taken orally in English or Spanish — but the Hazmat test is English-only.
Skills tests are English-only, and interpreters are prohibited for all tests.
Retest fees: $10 written, $20 skills. Initial CDL $75 plus $7 per endorsement, with a $6.25 service fee at tax collector offices.
There is no traffic-school point avoidance for CDL holders in Florida — convictions go straight on your record.

topics.heading: The one-week written-test plan
bullets: Day 1: Skim handbook Sections 1–3 + 11, take 2 General Knowledge practice tests, and log every miss by topic.
Day 2: Drill 4–6 General Knowledge tests until you hit 100% twice on two different sites; flashcard your misses.
Day 3: Air Brakes day — write the pressure ladder 20 times (125 cut-out / 100 cut-in / 55 warning / 20–45 spring brakes; 2-3-3-4 leak rates).
Day 4: Combination Vehicles — coupling/uncoupling steps, red vs blue lines, hand valve, fifth wheel, off-tracking.
Day 5: Full simulation — all three tests back-to-back, timed; book your FLHSMV appointment and start ELDT paperwork.
Day 6: Pre-trip script day — memorize the 7-step walk-around and say it out loud; re-take Air Brakes + Combination tests.
Day 7 (test day): One final pass of each practice test in the morning, arrive early, and use your 2 attempts if needed.
The night before: sleep. The morning of: caffeine, breakfast, and review your saved mistake list — not new material.

topics.heading: The trick numbers to drill (most-missed)
bullets: Air brakes: 125 psi governor cut-out, 100 psi cut-in, 55 psi low-air warning (or one-half governor cut-out on older vehicles), 20–45 psi spring brakes.
Leak rates: 2 psi/min single / 3 psi/min combo with brakes released; 3 psi/min single / 4 psi/min combo with the foot brake held.
Tread: 4/32 inch on steering tires, 2/32 inch on all others.
Following distance: 1 second per 10 feet of vehicle length under 40 mph, +1 second over 40 mph. A 40-ft truck needs 4 seconds; at 55 mph it's 5 seconds.
Stopping: 419 feet total at 55 mph; doubling your speed quadruples stopping distance.
Rail crossings: stop 15–50 feet from the nearest rail; a tractor-trailer needs about 14 seconds to clear a single track.
Red glad hand = emergency/supply line; blue = service line.
Cargo: re-check within the first 50 miles, then every 150 miles or 3 hours.

quiz.q: How many questions are on the Florida General Knowledge CDL test?
quiz.explain: 50 questions — you need 40 correct (80%) to pass.

quiz.q: How many correct answers do you need to pass the 50-question General Knowledge test?
quiz.explain: 80% of 50 = 40 correct.

quiz.q: A Class A applicant must pass which three knowledge tests?
options: General Knowledge, Combination Vehicles, Air Brakes
quiz.explain: General Knowledge (50 Q), Combination Vehicles (20 Q), and Air Brakes (25 Q) are the standard Class A set.

quiz.q: How many questions are on the Combination Vehicles test, and how many do you need correct?
quiz.explain: 20 questions with an 80% pass mark = 16 correct.

quiz.q: If you skip or fail the Air Brakes knowledge test, what restriction goes on your CDL?
quiz.explain: L = no air-brake-equipped CMV. If your truck has air brakes you must take and pass this test.

quiz.q: What happens if you take the skills test in an automatic transmission truck?
options: You get the E restriction (no manual transmission)
You must retake the written test
quiz.explain: Testing in an automatic (including AMTs) adds the E restriction. Test in a manual and you can drive both.

quiz.q: For the E restriction, an automated manual transmission (AMT) like an Eaton UltraShift counts as:
options: A manual only if you double-clutch
quiz.explain: Any transmission that doesn't operate fully on the gear-shift-and-clutch principle counts as automatic.

quiz.q: You already have a CDL with the E restriction. To remove it you must:
options: Retake all knowledge tests and ELDT
Pass a modified skills test in a manual truck
Wait 3 years with a clean record
Take a written manual-transmission test only
quiz.explain: Restriction removal uses a modified skills test — no ELDT and no full retest required.

quiz.q: How long must you hold your Florida CLP before taking the skills test?
quiz.explain: The CLP must be held 14 days before the skills test (federal rule).

quiz.q: What is ELDT and when is it required?
options: A written test you take online
Entry-Level Driver Training from an FMCSA-registered provider, required before your first skills test
quiz.explain: Since Feb 7, 2022, first-time CDL applicants must complete ELDT (theory, range, road) before the skills test.

quiz.q: How many attempts per test do you get in a single day in Florida?
quiz.explain: 2 attempts per test per day — and you can review your missed questions between attempts.

quiz.q: You fail the pre-trip inspection portion of the skills test. What happens?
options: You redo all three skills segments
You redo the road test only
quiz.explain: Fail the pre-trip and all three segments restart — FMCSA denied Florida's waiver request. This is why pre-trip practice matters most.

quiz.q: Which exercise is part of Florida's basic control skills test?
quiz.explain: Florida uses Forward Stop, Straight-Line Backing, Forward Offset Tracking, and Reverse Offset Backing.

quiz.q: A driver self-certifies as intrastate-only. What restriction applies?
quiz.explain: K = intrastate only. Under-21 drivers get it automatically; older drivers get it if they self-certify intrastate.

quiz.q: How many correct answers do you need on the 25-question Air Brakes test?
quiz.explain: 80% of 25 = 20 correct.

quiz.q: What's the most important reason to take your Class A skills test in a manual transmission truck?
options: You avoid the E restriction and can legally drive both manual and automatic trucks
Manual trucks are cheaper to rent
quiz.explain: Passing in a manual = no E restriction = you can drive both types. That's the entire reason to prefer manual.

tips.heading: The 7-day sprint, day by day
tips.body: Days 1–2: General Knowledge only. Take 2 practice tests, log every miss, drill until you hit 100% twice on two different sites. Day 3: Air Brakes — write the pressure ladder 20 times. Day 4: Combination Vehicles — coupling steps + air lines. Day 5: all three tests back-to-back, timed; book your FLHSMV appointment. Day 6: pre-trip script out loud + retake Air Brakes/Combination. Day 7: one calm pass of each test in the morning, then go take the real thing.

tips.heading: Don't chase the handbook — chase practice tests
tips.body: The #1 tip from r/Truckers: drill practice tests, not reading. Real questions come from a pool of roughly 100–200, and 25% swap between versions, so use 2–3 different sites. When you miss one, write down the topic and re-read only that subsection in the handbook.

tips.heading: The pre-trip is where Florida fails people
tips.body: Examiners score what they HEAR. Say every item out loud: 'not cracked, bent, broken, or illegally welded; properly mounted, no leaks, no missing or damaged parts.' Walk the same clockwise pattern every time, and do the 3-part air brake check verbatim — skipping a step fails the whole inspection.
